A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ConvSearch-R1 study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison. v2 retains the earlier material and adds Appendices F–G.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval experiments on TopiOCQA and QReCC, including transfer evaluations, ablations, scaling experiments, and reward comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds results using RepLLaMA, TREC CAsT benchmarks, and latency measurements in Tables 8–10.

M1.justification: Both versions use self-distillation and rank-1 filtering for policy warm-up, followed by GRPO with rank-incentive rewards and a format penalty. Figure 2 and notation changes clarify this existing procedure. The additional retriever experiments do not introduce a new algorithm component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates TopiOCQA and QReCC, including transfer between them. v2 retains this coverage and adds evaluation on TREC CAsT 2019, 2020, and 2021 without training explicitly on those benchmarks, substantially broadening independent test coverage.

E2.justification: The original comparison sets remain. Table 9 adds previously unevaluated comparators: RepLLaMA, E5-Mistral, LLM-Embedder, HyDE, Query2doc, and InstructorR. These are reported comparison rows, substantially expanding the comparator set beyond merely extending existing baselines to another benchmark.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce RepLLaMA retrieval and vLLM timing measurements of output length, total time, and seconds per sample. Table 10 reports 2,514 TopiOCQA and 8,209 QReCC timing samples; the latter differs without explanation from the retained 8,124-query dataset statistic. Previously stated training settings and retrieval metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices F–G add retriever robustness checks, further held-out transfer evaluations, and output-length/latency analysis. These extend the supplementary analysis while retaining the existing component ablations, warm-up trajectories, reward comparisons, scaling analysis, and case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The added retrieval and timing tables continue reporting point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Earlier result values are retained, while Tables 8–10 add substantial results under new settings. TREC CAsT MRR@3 is reported as 76.6, 70.6, and 73.2 for 2019–2021. New latency estimates are 0.049 and 0.053 seconds per sample on TopiOCQA and QReCC. These are additional findings rather than improvements to the same v1 experiments.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and objectives remain substantively unchanged. Equation 1 adjusts the second mapping's interval notation, whose lower endpoint was already excluded by its indicator; Equation 2 adds missing set braces. Figure 2 now displays the existing piecewise reward explicitly. No new theory or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about eliminating external rewrite supervision, two-stage retrieval alignment, smaller models, and strong retrieval performance. The appendix experiments supply additional support without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix F interprets the new results as evidence of applicability to a newer retriever and unseen benchmarks. Appendix G characterizes the reasoning overhead as acceptable and latency as close to RETPO. Earlier mechanism explanations and the stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix G newly identifies vLLM as the framework used for latency measurements. Existing training hyperparameters, prompts, model access links, and code/data availability statements remain. Hardware and batching details for the new timing experiment are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds the three Dalton et al. TREC CAsT references, Ma et al. on RepLLaMA, and Kwon et al. on vLLM. These support the added experiments; Section 2 and Appendix A retain the earlier research positioning and novelty arguments.

P1.justification: v2 expands abbreviations, clarifies the initial model and sample notation, makes local wording corrections, and adds acknowledgments and Appendices F–G. The existing narrative and section organization are largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds three appendix tables and revises Figure 2's indexing, reward display, and labels. Existing appendix displays move with the reflow; the earlier case-study Table 8 becomes Table 11. The main plots and overall visual format remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The newer-retriever and TREC CAsT evaluations broaden support for generalization, while latency measurements partly address v1's unquantified computational-overhead limitation. The benefit is limited by missing timing hardware/batching details and overbroad interpretation: on CAsT 2020, R@10 is 15.6 versus 19.3 for LLM4CS and CHIQ-Fusion, despite Appendix F.2's language about consistent superiority. The additions provide useful but incompletely documented validation.
